stem: Trap counts stay low, yet direct plant inspections repeatedly find a nonflying pest increasing on lower leaf surfaces. What is the strongest conclusion?
choices: The direct observations must be wrong because traps are objective
The monitoring program needs methods matched to the organism; one trap type cannot represent every pest pathway or life stage
All traps should be removed permanently
The pest population cannot be increasing unless flying adults are also counted
rationale: Monitoring tools detect different organisms and life stages with different sensitivity. Direct scouting remains important when the pest is poorly represented by the trap method.
